title: The builder-test-edit guard does not refuse a builder's plain run of a test file; it only refuses writes
why: Lane shared-savings-gap-read via the coordinator 01:03 CST Nov 14 (relayed; the builder's hand-back in that lane is the evidence, unread by triage): the guard rule builder-test-edit refused a builder agent's plain `python3 lint/test_rule_audit.py` run (a call that only runs the test) twice, about 00:14 CST. How often is unmeasured.
source: Lane message 01:03 CST Nov 14 (relayed). Same family, not the same cause as read: builder-test-edit-label-words (todo: an env-assignment value or label words read as a test-file write), write-then-run-test-edit (done: a script an agent wrote gets the interpreter check when Bash runs it). The refusal text was not given.
note: Triage 01:05 CST Nov 14: mistake the guard stops: a builder editing tests (the builder's role bars it). The false alarm: running a test. Fix: red first: a builder's `python3 lint/test_<name>.py` with no write to a test path passes; control: a write to a test file by a builder still refuses. The lane first gets the refusal text and the hand-back, and says whether the cause is the interpreter check, the words, or something else, and whether this step folds into builder-test-edit-label-words. A guard change: own lane, review rounds apply. Not started. Refusal read 01:10 CST Nov 14 (lane shared-savings-gap-read, from the builder transcript; unchecked by triage): builder agent (sonnet), about 00:13 CST, Bash `/root/.claude/bin/verdict python3 lint/test_rule_audit.py`, refused twice with: "PreToolUse:Bash hook error: builder-test-edit: A builder does not change tests or test config. Report the needed test change in your report. The orchestrator assigns it to a test-author. A merge conflict in a test file takes the same route. (decision builders-cannot-edit-tests, a builder never changes a test or test config) No override lifts this refusal." The orchestrator ran the same command in its own checkout at head 99a8fb852 and it passed (PASS, 9.9 s): a plain test run. The command runs through `verdict`, which the refusal text does not mention; so the cause (the interpreter check on `python3 lint/test_*.py`, the `verdict` wrapper, or the path words) is still unread.  Second sighting 04:04 CST Nov 14 (lane priority-vs-merge-order, relayed 04:04): a possible false alarm: the hook refuses even a read-only run of lint/test_rule_audit.py for a builder. Same class as the first sighting.
